(The passage here is free now until the end of the year.)
Marcos said the opening of the Segment 8.2 Section 1A was done in time for the Undas exodus to alleviate the traffic for motorists and passengers.

"Kahit maikli lang, dalawang kilometro, napakalaking bagay dahil ang dinadaanan ngayon ay napakalayo bago umiikot at pabababa sa surface road, dadaanan ng traffic, siguro 40 to 45 minutes ngayon. Pagbukas nito, 5 minuto na lang," he said.

(Even though it's short—just two kilometers—it makes a huge difference, because the current route is very long. You have to go around and pass the surface road, where you encounter traffic, so it probably takes 40 to 45 minutes right now. Once this opens, it will only take 5 minutes.)
The President also said the MVP Group, in coordination with SM Group, will be investing P120 billion for a project to connect Balintawak to Bocaue, Bulacan.
"Maglalagay sila ng elevated na daan mula Balintawak hanggang Bocaue. Napakalaking bagay nito dahil ito ay idadaan nila doon sa may highway na ngayon, maglalagay sila ng elevated," Marcos said.

(They will construct an elevated road from Balintawak to Bocaue. This is a major development because it will be built above the existing highway. They are going to put up an elevated structure there.)

"Ibang iba ang magiging karanasan, ang traveling experience para sa mga commuter natin kapag natapos na 'yan. Napakalaking investment na gagawin ng MVP Group at siyempre kasama nila ang SM Group dahil kailangan nilang mag-coordinate," he added.

(The travel experience of our commuters will be completely different once that is completed. It is a massive investment by the MVP Group, in collaboration with the SM Group, as they need to coordinate with each other.)
— VDV, GMA News

articles.title: Ex-BARMM MP Rimbang to appear before PDEA probe into Laos drug shipment on Nov. 5
articles.summary: Former Bangsamoro parliament member Edrieza Hadji Nasser Rimbang is expected to appear before the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) on November 5, the agency said Thursday.

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 11:26am
Former Bangsamoro parliament member Edrieza Hadji Nasser Rimbang is expected to appear before the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) on November 5, the agency said Thursday.
Rimbang has been linked to the attempted smuggling of P3.5-billion illegal drugs from Laos to the Philippines.

“The lawyers of Sultan Rimbang came to our office the other day and they committed to present him sa opisina po natin on November 5,” PDEA spokesperson Joseph Frederick Calulut told reporters in an phone patch interview.
(The lawyers of Sultan Rimbang came to our office the other day and they committed to present him on November 5.)
Rimbang is one of the 11 persons of interest in the case who received a subpoena from authorities. Two persons of interest have yet to report to authorities.

According to Calulut, the lawyers did not explain why Rimbang failed to immediately appear at the PDEA’s office amid allegations that the he was the alleged financier and mastermind in the drug smuggling operation.
Calulut said PDEA continues to consider Rimbang a suspected mastermind behind the drug shipment based on the evidence available to investigators.

“Based on the evidence on hand, he appears to be the mastermind. Hindi lang siya financial. Pero we are still waiting for him to come to our office to give his statement para at least 'yung statement niya, hindi lang pang-social media. Dito na, mas maganda naka-affidavit na ‘to siya,” he said.

(Based on the evidence on hand, he appears to be the mastermind. He's not just for financial. But we are still waiting for him to come to our office to give his statement so at least his statement is not just for social media. Here, it's better if he has an affidavit.)
PDEA has documents and other evidence indicating that Rimbang provided the money for the shipment, according to Calulut.
He said the agency was still checking Rimbang's background and possible previous links to illegal drugs.
Earlier, Rimbang denied involvement in the attempted smuggling.
“Wala po itong katotohanan (there is no truth to this),” he said in a video posted on his social media page.
On October 1, Lao authorities thwarted P3.5 billion in illegal drugs on a private plane headed to the Philippines. —AOL, GMA News

articles.title: US: Department of Homeland Security data leak exposes details of more than 40,000 employees
articles.summary: The leaked information reportedly includes names, phone numbers and email addresses of personnel across several US security agencies. This follows recent data breaches involving the FBI and the…

image.caption: DHS said it was working to ensure its employees were properly protected and would update the public 'when more information is available' [FILE: September 19, 2025]Image: Erin Hooley/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: In the third major US government data leak in the past month, details on more than 40,000 US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) employees, including officials involved in surveillance, intelligence and undercover operations, were released on Wednesday by a nonprofit leak website.

Distributed Denial of Secrets, a nonprofit data transparency group, said the data was obtained by an entity calling itself "Department of Peace" and provided to the group and "journalist and hacktivist maia arson crimew."

DHS said in a statement that it was "aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively." The agency said it would provide further updates when more information became available.
Transparency group says releasing data justified
The leaked DHS data reportedly includes names, phone numbers and email addresses of personnel from:

items: Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)
Customs and Border Protection (CBP)
US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS)
Homeland Security Investigations (HSI)
the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
​other DHS agencies

blocks.text: The data transparency group also provided a link to an online search tool that helps the public sift through the data.
Distributed Denial of Secrets co-founder Emma Best said the leak identifies "key personnel in DHS' ever-escalating rendition and deportation programs," according to a statement on their website.
Best said the tool would "replace anonymity with accountability" and aid journalists as well as facilitate congressional oversight.
According to Reuters, the news agency called three DHS employees based on the data and was able to confirm their phone numbers and other details.

DHS said in September that it was initiating a "surge in sanctuary cities," which are known to limit cooperation with federal authorities — as the Trump administration ramped up its crackdown on immigration.
The non-partisan Migration Policy Institute said in a fact sheet that the DHS has expanded its arrests and deportations over the last several months.
Third serious data breach recently
This is the third major US government data breach in recent weeks:

items: Last week, the Defense Department faced a class-action lawsuit over a breach affecting millions of current and former military personnel
In September, hacking group ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen data of thousands of Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) employees.

articles.title: Chagee’s new drinks use espresso shots, but with tea
articles.summary: A new way of espresso with cha, g (Chagee)?

blocks.text: Whether it’s a cup of tea or a hit of caffeine, we all need that morning and midday energizer. As Chagee expands its Teaspresso lineup, you can now get your daily dose of both caffeine and tea in one drink.
We had the chance to try some of Chagee’s newly released Teaspresso drinks. Here’s what to expect from each one to help you find your next go-to order.

Frappe, Latte, Or Tea? Don’t worry, as Chagee has you covered. Each drink differs in its base: a milk base for your latte, a water base for your tea, and a blended one for your frappe. Despite their different profiles, they all share a shot of “teaspresso,” or in simple words, tea leaves that were extracted through an espresso-style brewing method, meaning you’re sure to get both flavors of tea and its extracted caffeine.

One distinct change from the menu is their new Frappe-style drink. For a sweeter touch, the teaspresso blended in the drink gives a subtle hint of caffeine while highlighting the base of each flavor being either caramel or chocolate cookie. Topped with whipped cream, it finishes with a smooth, dessert-like texture that makes it feel like your needed sugar boost. It’s a good pick if you want something sweeter, yet balanced with the taste of tea and caffeine.

To get a full experience of the Teaspresso, Chagee’s pure tea drink pairs a shot with a water base, making the tea stand as its core flavor. Compared to the others, this one places itself on the calmer side, focusing on the flavors of tea rather than added flavors or sugar. If you’re looking for a simple drink that’s not too sweet or plain, or simply in the mood for some tea, Teaspresso Pure Tea is the perfect choice.

Despite having no coffee, the Teaspresso latte had a faint yet distinguishable taste of caffeine. With a milk base and a shot of Teaspresso, it lands between something familiar to my go-to cafe latte in the morning and surprising given its gentle lift without tipping into a full coffee profile. For the coffee lovers, this is a nice middle ground for satisfying your daily caffeine while also getting a hint of tea.

Chagee’s new Teaspresso drinks brought different flavor profiles to their signature taste, assuring that whether you’re a tea or coffee person, or someone with a sweet tooth, you’re sure to find the right drink for you. Will you stick to your usual, or try something new on your next Chagee run? – Rappler.com

This piece was written by Rappler intern Sebastian Vincent U. Ngo. Basti is a multimedia creative storyteller who focuses on the everyday details that make ordinary moments feel special. He seeks stories and uses design, words, and motion to help people see the familiar in a new light.

articles.title: Milwaukee Brewers defeat Tampa Bay Rays to become 1st-time World Series champions
articles.summary: The scrappy Milwaukee Brewers captured the franchise's first World Series title, defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla., Wednesday.

image.caption: William Contreras of the Milwaukee Brewers reacts after hitting an RBI double in the sixth inning of Game 5 of the World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays. The Brewers won the game 4-1 — to clinch the overall championship on Wednesday night. (Mike Stobe/Getty Images)

blocks.text: MLB·Breaking
The small-ball Milwaukee Brewers playing in the smallest market in the majors are World Series champions for the first time in franchise history.
Milwaukee defeated Tampa 4-1 in Game 5 of the World Series at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla.
Hey, Milwaukee: raise a beer and prepare for that parade.

Young ace Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings of two-hit ball, rookie Cooper Pratt got two more hits and two RBIs, and the Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday night to set off a long-awaited celebration among thousands of Brewers fans in attendance at Tropicana Field.
Members of the Tampa Bay Rays watch during the ninth inning of Game 5 of the World Series, which the team lost to the Brewers. (Kim Klement Neitzel/Imagn Images/Reuters)
Misiorowski left the game because of a right calf cramp. He got a standing ovation from the Brew-Crew fans, who took over the section behind Milwaukee's dugout for the last three games.
The 22-year-old Pratt set a Series rookie record with six straight hits before a sacrifice fly in the sixth inning. Jackson Chourio set a five-game Series record with 11 hits.

The World Series title comes in the 58th season for a franchise that began as the Seattle Pilots in 1969 and moved to Milwaukee the following year. The Brewers' only previous trip to the World Series in 1982 ended in heartbreak when they blew a 3-1 lead in the sixth inning of Game 7 and lost 6-3 to the St. Louis Cardinals.
More to come.

articles.title: Philippines, India pledge deeper defense ties
articles.summary: The Philippines and India pledged on Wednesday to deepen defense cooperation, with Manila moving to post a liaison officer at an Indian Navy-run maritime information center.

blocks.text: October 29, 2026 | 11:11am

The Philippines and India reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral defense cooperation, with maritime security, defense modernization, and military engagements among the key areas discussed during the meeting between Department of National Defense (DND) Secretary Gilberto C. Teodoro Jr. and Indian Minister of Defence Rajnath Singh on the sidelines of the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026.
Department of National Defense

MANILA, Philippines — The Philippines and India pledged on Wednesday, October 28, to deepen defense cooperation, with Manila moving to post a liaison officer at an Indian Navy-run maritime information center.
Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. made the commitment during talks with Indian Defense Minister Rajnath Singh in Cebu, where the Philippines is hosting the 13th ASEAN Defense Ministers' Meeting.
The center, known as the Information Fusion Centre–Indian Ocean Region, tracks shipping and maritime security incidents and shares the data with partner navies.
Teodoro committed to "facilitating the deployment" of a Philippine officer there "to strengthen maritime information-sharing," according to a statement from the Department of National Defense.
Joint defense production
Singh said both sides also discussed the possibility of "joint defense production," among others.

"We reviewed our ongoing defense cooperation and discussed avenues to further strengthen our strategic partnership, particularly focusing on maritime security and joint defense production," he said in a post on X.

The talks built on ties the two countries raised to a strategic partnership in August 2025, during President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.'s state visit to New Delhi. India became the Philippines' fifth strategic partner.
Marcos said at the time that the partnership opened "a new era of closer, multidimensional, and impactful engagement."
India also invited the Philippines to join the information center during that visit.
Defense ties between both sides have also centered on the BrahMos, a supersonic cruise missile that India builds with Russia.
In January 2022, Manila signed a deal worth about $375 million for three shore-based anti-ship missile batteries for the Philippine Marine Corps.
Deliveries began in April 2024, which led the Philippines to test the missiles in a simulated strike at sea during this year's Balikatan exercises with the United States.
In Cebu, Singh "highlighted the progress" of the BrahMos project under the military's modernization program, according to the DND.
The two navies held their first joint sail in the West Philippine Sea in August 2025, the part of the South China Sea that falls within the Philippines' exclusive economic zone.

China, which claims almost the entire waterway, sent its own patrols during the drills. Its foreign ministry reacted to the patrols and said "no third party is in any position to interfere" in the disputes.
A 2016 arbitral ruling under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) found that Beijing's sweeping claims in the South China Sea had no legal basis. China rejects the decision.
On Wednesday, Singh stressed freedom of navigation and "upholding the principles reflected in" UNCLOS, the DND said.
India has cited the 2016 arbitral award in joint statements with Manila since 2023.
Ship visits, working group vs terrorism
Singh also pointed to reciprocal ship visits, staff talks between the two militaries and the setting up of a joint working group on counterterrorism.
The Indian official cited two exercises held at Subic Bay in late September, including the second ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise, which the two countries co-hosted.
Teodoro, for his part, pushed to expand the Philippine defense attaché's office in India. The DND said this would allow "broader engagement" with India's defense institutions and military services.
He also thanked India for helping Filipinos in the Indian Ocean and the Persian Gulf.

articles.title: Palace urges Congress not to cut Marcos projects in 2027 budget
articles.summary: The Palace said previous cuts redirected funds to unprogrammed appropriations.

blocks.text: October 29, 2026 | 10:40am
Presidential Press Officer Claire Castro speaks at a briefing in Cagayan de Oro on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026.
PCO

MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang urged Congress to preserve projects proposed by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in the P7.2-trillion national budget for 2027 as previous cuts redirected funds to unprogrammed appropriations.
Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said the Supreme Court's recent ruling should guide lawmakers as they complete next year's spending plan.

"What the Supreme Court said should really be followed," Castro said in an interview with Bombo Radyo Cagayan de Oro on Wednesday, October 28. She added that projects proposed by the administration should no longer be reduced.
The House of Representatives has approved its version of the budget, while deliberations remain underway in the Senate.
Castro said lawmakers should avoid departing from the executive's proposal so that the administration's planned projects can be carried out.
"The power of the purse is with Congress. What the executive submits is only a proposed budget," she said.

She also defended the Marcos administration's handling of previous budgets, saying the Department of Budget and Management had been cautious in releasing money for projects whose proponents failed to provide sufficient justification.
That caution contributed to slower government spending in 2025, which the economic team and the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas said weighed on economic activity, according to Castro.
Asked whether the House should revisit its approved version of the 2027 budget, Castro said that decision rested with Congress.
She also urged lawmakers to consider the legislative timetable as they decide how to respond to the Supreme Court ruling.
"We will not interfere with what they want to do there," she said. "But perhaps they should also look at the time."

Budget watchdogs have meanwhile also criticized the House version of the budget. The People's Budget Coalition told the Senate that it found more than P1 trillion in what it called budget "red flags," including P695 billion in politically driven infrastructure, P210 billion in patronage-prone assistance programs and P112 billion in unprogrammed appropriations.
The coalition also flagged nearly 7,000 infrastructure projects worth P190 billion that it said were added without publicly available supporting documents.

articles.title: US to boost security aid for AFP modernization
articles.summary: The additional security cooperation funds are meant to accelerate the modernization of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and enhance interoperability "along the First Island Chain," the…

blocks.text: October 29, 2026 | 10:36am

In this photo taken on March 28, 2026, US marines reloading ammunition on a Marine Air Defence Integrated system (MADIS) launcher during the integrated missile exercise as part of the Balikatan joint Philippines and US military exercise at a naval base facing South China Sea in San Antonio, Zambales province.
AFP / Ted Aljibe

MANILA, Philippines — The United States will raise its funding support for the Philippines' military modernization program, which Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. has said is "stuck" with a P50-billion allocation because of the existing modernization law.

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced the increase at a meeting with Teodoro on Wednesday, October 28, according to a readout from the US Department of War, as the Trump administration now calls the Pentagon.
The talks were held on the sidelines of the ASEAN Defense Ministers' Meeting in Cebu.

The additional security cooperation funds are meant to accelerate the modernization of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and enhance interoperability "along the First Island Chain," the readout said.
The First Island Chain refers to the arc of islands from Japan through Taiwan and the Philippines that US military planners see as central to deterring China.
It did not say how large the increase would be or when the money would be released.
The two officials also agreed to launch an "alliance command and control modernization sprint" to improve real-time coordination between their forces.
Both sides welcomed progress at sites covered by the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement, including investments in infrastructure and storage facilities across the country.

The Pentagon funds are separate from the Foreign Military Financing (FMF) grants the US Congress has approved for Manila. The 2026 US National Defense Authorization Act, which President Donald Trump signed in December 2025, allows up to $500 million a year in FMF for the Philippines from 2026 to 2030 — on its own more than half of the P50 billion Manila has proposed for modernization next year — plus up to $1 billion in direct loans.
For fiscal year 2026, Congress appropriated at least $100 million in FMF grants for the Philippines, according to the Congressional Research Service.
At home, officials say the AFP's modernization fund has fallen well short of what the country needs as it looks to shore up its territorial defense capabilities and defense posture at sea.

The proposed 2027 national budget sets aside P50 billion for the Revised AFP Modernization Program, up from P40 billion in regular funds this year but less than 40% of the P126.97 billion the Department of National Defense (DND) told the House of Representatives in August that it requires.
The DND's overall budget for 2027 was set at P324.63 billion, about 43% less than the P572.79 billion it requested. Its capital outlay was cut to P32.67 billion from the P239.73 billion it sought.
Before a Senate finance subcommittee on October 19, Teodoro said Horizon 3, the modernization program's third and final phase, needs at least P70 billion.
If all planned projects were contracted, he said, the DND would need P20 billion on top of the P50 billion just to pay for multi-year contracts.
Republic Act 10349, or the Revised AFP Modernization Act, was enacted in 2012 as a 15-year program split into three phases and is set to conclude in 2027.

Teodoro has repeatedly urged Congress to repeal the law and argued its set cycles cannot keep pace with military technology. He also says its intended funding source — remittances from the Bases Conversion and Development Authority — has been marginal and has had to be subsidized by the national government.
"Which entity works on 15-year horizons in this day and age?" he said in an August statement.
Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian said on Thursday he is pushing for a bigger AFP budget to sustain the military's modernization, readiness and capability-building.

"Our geopolitical situation in the region and around the world is changing very quickly. We can see the other conflicts in the Middle East and Eastern Europe," Gatchalian said in Filipino at the Senate hearing on the DND budget, according to a statement from his office.
"At this point, it is important that we are prepared and continue to modernize and strengthen our armed forces, including their capacity for cyber warfare," he added.

articles.title: ‘They mobilized a whole government response to that joke’: Obama laughs off Trump attacks in rally for Ossoff
articles.summary:
Former US president comes to Georgia to support Jon Ossoff for US Senate and Keisha Lance Bottoms for governor

Barack Obama, speaking at a Wednesday campaign rally in suburban Atlanta,…

blocks.text: Barack Obama, speaking at a Wednesday campaign rally in suburban Atlanta, offered a closing argument for Democrats in the final week of the midterm election campaign.
“These are not serious people,” he said of Donald Trump and the Republican party. “And we’re all paying the price for their lack of seriousness.”

Obama came to Georgia to support the campaigns of US senator Jon Ossoff, former Atlanta mayor and gubernatorial hopeful Keisha Lance Bottoms, and an array of down-ballot Democrats as part of his cross-country campaign tour before next week’s election. From 3,500 to 4,000 people filled the Discovery Center of Clayton county for the late election season stop, just south of Atlanta.

Obama has been casting caltrops behind him with each campaign stop, offering pointed criticism of Republican candidates and Donald Trump that has been unusual for the former president. He continued to do so on Wednesday, again invoking the image of Trump’s gilded renovations of the White House and noting Trump’s strident reaction to his crack last week likening it to Saddam Hussein decorating a Cheesecake Factory.

“The Saddam Hussein thing didn’t bother him. But he was very upset about the Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said. “I mean, it’s all crazy, but this is the crazy part: they mobilized a whole government response to that joke.

“The White House even called the secretary of the treasury,” the former president continued. “The guy who is trying to figure out how to lower inflation … they told him he should hold a press conference in front of the Cheesecake Factory.”
He also rebuffed Republicans’ accusations of snobbery for referencing the popular chain restaurant.
“I am the father of two daughters,” Obama said. “Do you think I could have survived their childhood without going to the Cheesecake Factory?”
But he turned that discussion to the problems of affordability for American voters, in contrast with the corruption of the presidency.
“We have never seen a president so intent on selling favors,” Obama said. “The guy has made billions of dollars while in office. Understand that this has not been done in modern times.”
The construction of a new ballroom on the site of the former East Wing of the White House featured in the comments of many speakers at Wednesday’s rally, including Ossoff.
“Each day, Donald Trump digs the moral pit deeper,” Ossoff said, accusing the president of leading “the most corrupt administration of all time, and everybody knows it”.

“If you’re involved in any of this, next year you’ll be raising your hand to tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth,” Ossoff said, in reference to Democrats pledging to impeach Trump if they take control of Congress next year.
The crowd chanted: “Lock him up!” in response.

Bottoms, meanwhile, contrasted her candidacy with that of her Republican opponent Rick Jackson, tying the billionaire healthcare executive to Trump and describing them as “two out-of-touch billionaires who want to keep getting rich on the backs of taxpayers”.

Invoking the legacies of US Representative John Lewis and Coretta Scott King, Bottoms characterized her candidacy as transcending politics. “They may have the money, but they will never overtake our movement,” she said.

Despite a broad wave of Democratic support buoying candidates across the country – and the eight- to 10-point polling lead Ossoff has on his Republican opponent, US Representative Mike Collins – Bottoms is statistically tied in polls with Jackson. If elected, Bottoms would break the state’s Republican trifecta – where the GOP has controlled both chambers of the legislature and the governor’s office – which began in 2004.
Rev Raphael Warnock, Georgia’s other senator, warned of “spiritual wickedness in high places” while describing the effects of deep cuts to Medicaid and Snap nutrition support for children.

“This is about the character of the country,” Warnock said. “This is about who we are and whether we are here for one another … I am concerned about the spiritual health of our country. There is brokenness, because only a broken nation could manage to elect Donald Trump twice.”

Trump, who was campaigning in Ohio at the same time as the Georgia rally, has also been on a national rally blitz, holding near-daily events in the final days of the midterm campaign. Trump has made two appearances in as many weeks in Georgia, both in what would otherwise seem to be congressional districts that are safe territory for Republicans.

articles.title: Utah files criminal charges against prediction market Kalshi and company co-founders
articles.summary:
Firm calls charges, which include violating state gambling ban and profiting from illegal activity, ‘crazy overreach’

Utah on Wednesday filed criminal charges against prediction market…

blocks.text: Utah on Wednesday filed criminal charges against prediction market operator Kalshi and two of its executives, months after a federal judge rejected Kalshi’s effort to prevent Utah from enforcing its strict anti-gambling laws against the activity.
The felony charges could represent a new tactic in how states try to assert regulatory authority over the fast-expanding activity, a clash that appears headed to a showdown at the US supreme court.
The charges include 13 counts of violating the state’s prohibition on gambling and another charge involving profiting off illegal activity.
The state’s charging documents name Kalshi and its co-founders, chief executive officer Tarek Mansour and chief operating officer Luana Lopes Lara.
In a statement, Utah attorney general Derek Brown said Kalshi has continued to operate in Utah, despite a federal court ruling that Utah’s gambling laws apply to the company.

“Gambling is illegal in Utah, whether you place the bet, run the game, or promote it. Calling it a ‘prediction market’ doesn’t change what it is, and being federally registered doesn’t put a company above the law,” Brown said in a statement.
The attorney general’s office did not immediately say what sort of criminal penalties it would seek in the case, although the felony charges carry the possibility of jail time.
In a statement, Kalshi called the charges a “crazy overreach” and said that “Utah is clearly playing politics”.
“We look forward to putting a stop to this in court, just like we did in Arizona,” it said.

Utah has been on the front lines of a battle between states and the federal government over who regulates the markets. Litigation has spread across roughly 20 states, creating a fragmented legal landscape that analysts say will likely be settled by the supreme court.
Kalshi has maintained that prediction markets fall exclusively under federal jurisdiction and are not governed by state gambling laws.

articles.title: The bee is strong: Jollibee eyes 1,500 more areas for expansion
articles.summary: The fast-food giant sees more room to grow outside Metro Manila, while setting its sights on listing its international business in Hong Kong in 2027

blocks.text: The fast-food giant sees more room to grow outside Metro Manila, while setting its sights on listing its international business in Hong Kong in 2027

items: Jollibee Foods Corporation plans to expand by identifying over 1,500 potential areas for growth in the Philippines from 2027 to 2030, primarily outside Metro Manila.

The company's three main brands—Jollibee, Mang Inasal, and Chowking—account for nearly 90% of its Philippine sales, with Jollibee contributing 62%. However, the identified areas do not guarantee new store openings.
JFC is also preparing to spin off its international operations into a separate entity, Jollibee Foods Corporation International, with a potential listing in Hong Kong by late 2027.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – The bee still has plenty of room to grow.
Fast-food giant Jollibee Foods Corporation (JFC) has identified more than 1,500 potential areas for expansion across the Philippines from 2027 to 2030, with most of these outside Metro Manila.

In a disclosure on Thursday, October 29, JFC said approximately 71% of these prospective markets are outside the capital region, where the company sees considerable room to grow its Jollibee, Mang Inasal, and Chowking brands.
The three brands already account for nearly 90% of its Philippine systemwide sales, with Jollibee alone contributing more than half at 62%.
But the 1,500 identified trade areas do not necessarily translate to 1,500 new stores.

The company has yet to disclose specific locations, investment requirements, or annual store-opening targets associated with its expansion plans. Actual openings will depend on site availability, commercial viability, and expected investment returns, JFC said.
The expansion outlook comes after JFC revised down its global store opening target for 2026 from 1,200 to 1,300 new stores to just 1,000 to 1,100 in its Q2 2026 updated full-year guidance.
JFC’s Philippine business reported 5.7% growth in systemwide sales during Q2 2026, while same-store sales, which measure performance at existing outlets, grew a more modest 1.3%.
Beyond opening new stores, JFC is also experimenting with different formats to improve sales.
The company reported that Mang Inasal’s eight drive-thru outlets operating as of the first half of 2026 generated average daily sales approximately 40% higher than those of its other stores.

blocks.caption: How Jollibee became Filipino food’s biggest ambassador in the US

blocks.text: Meanwhile, Jollibee has been happy to play part-time ambassador too.

When President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. visited Canada in July, he and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney also made a stop at a Jollibee branch in Vancouver, where they mingled with customers and employees after their bilateral meetings.

blocks.caption: PRESIDENTIAL VISIT. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. visit a Jollibee store in Vancouver on July 2, 2026 following a bilateral meeting between the two leaders. Photo from Presidential Communications Office

blocks.text: Two months later, British Trade Minister Anas Sarwar dropped by a Jollibee store in Bonifacio Global City during the first visit by a UK trade minister to the Philippines in nine years. He met JFC founder Tony Tan Caktiong, sampled the menu, and even received a Jollibee Funko Pop dressed in a Barong Tagalog.

blocks.caption: MABUHAY! UK Trade Minister Anas Sarwar (second from left) and British Ambassador Sarah Hulton (second from right) meet Jollibee founder Tony Tan Caktiong (center) and executive William Tan Untiong (right) at a Jollibee store in BGC on September 23, 2026. Photo from Jollibee.

blocks.text: The bee, it seems, is becoming quite the fixture in international relations.
And its international ambitions extend to the stock market.

JFC is preparing to spin off its international operations into a separately listed company, Jollibee Foods Corporation International (JFCI), with Hong Kong selected as its proposed listing venue instead of the United States, as originally planned.

Under the proposed restructuring, the Philippine business would remain listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange, while investors would be able to hold shares in a separately traded international company.

JFC is looking at a potential listing by late 2027, although it clarified on October 20 that reports of a Q3 2027 listing target were premature. The transaction remains subject to restructuring, market conditions, and regulatory approvals.
As of the first half of 2026, JFC operated 3,516 stores in the Philippines and another 7,251 internationally. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Bato says P50-million bounty puts life at risk, asks Supreme Court to block arrest
articles.summary: Sen. Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa has asked the Supreme Court anew to stop his arrest, saying the P50-million bounty for his capture and his designation as "armed and dangerous" put his life in "serious…

blocks.text: October 29, 2026 | 9:34am
Sen. Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa attends the Senate session on Monday, May 11, 2026, hours before being placed under Senate protective custody amid reports of an alleged ICC arrest warrant.
Senate PRIB

MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa has asked the Supreme Court (SC) anew to stop his arrest, saying the P50-million bounty for his capture and his designation as "armed and dangerous" put his life in "serious danger."

In a 15-page manifestation filed with the high court, Dela Rosa, through lawyer Israelito Torreon, asked the SC to reverse its May 2026 denial of his request for a temporary restraining order (TRO) or status quo ante order against the implementation of the International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrant.

Torreon cited recent developments that he said warranted the issuance of a TRO, including the P50-million bounty announced by Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla on October 23 and the police's declaration that the senator was "armed and dangerous."
The government also gave Dela Rosa until Thursday, October 29, to surrender.

The manifestation cited Remulla's announcement that authorities were abandoning their previous approach of negotiation, as well as Malacañang's statement that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. had directed law enforcement agencies to act swiftly to capture the senator.

"Taken together, these are not stray remarks of individual officials. They constitute an announced executive enforcement program all directed at the arrest of a sitting senator of the Republic for surrender to a foreign tribunal, while the legality of that very act is pending before this Honorable Court," the manifestation read.
Dela Rosa said the bounty and the government's actions placed his right to life at risk, particularly amid the possibility of armed resistance during his arrest.

He also asked the SC to stop authorities from surrendering him to the ICC, which issued an arrest warrant against him in November 2025 over alleged crimes against humanity linked to former president Rodrigo Duterte's drug war.

Palace press officer Claire Castro on Tuesday defended the P50-million bounty, clarifying that the money would come from the Department of the Interior and Local Government's intelligence and confidential funds, not from Marcos.
Castro said the DILG and the Philippine National Police have their own mandates and funding for operations, adding that the reward was intended to speed up Dela Rosa's capture.
She said the deadline was meant to give the senator an opportunity to surrender without police intervention. However, she warned that authorities would hunt him down if he refused to cooperate.

Dela Rosa has been in hiding since May, when authorities attempted to serve the ICC warrant against him. He emerged from hiding on May 11 and took refuge inside the Senate building but left days later following a standoff between security guards and investigators attempting to arrest him. Shots were fired during the incident.
In May, the SC denied Dela Rosa's request for a TRO or status quo ante order in a 9-5-1 vote, ruling that he had "no clear and unmistakable right to be protected."
The high court has yet to rule on his petition challenging the legality of the ICC warrant.
ICC prosecutors have named Dela Rosa as one of eight alleged co-perpetrators in the drug crackdown, which killed thousands of suspected drug offenders during Duterte's presidency from 2016 to 2022.

Duterte was arrested in Manila on March 11, 2025, and transferred to the ICC the following day. He remains detained at the ICC detention center in The Hague, the Netherlands, and is scheduled to stand trial on Nov. 30, 2026, on charges of crimes against humanity of murder. — with a report from Alyana Uy

articles.title: Talks to replace VP Sara Duterte amid impeachment trial 'premature' -spox
articles.summary: Discussions on possible replacements for Vice President Sara Duterte are premature and a distraction from serious issues surrounding the impeachment trial, her spokesperson said Thursday.

blocks.text: Published October 29, 2026 9:28am
Discussions on possible replacements for Vice President Sara Duterte are premature and a distraction from serious issues surrounding the impeachment trial, her spokesperson said Thursday.

In a statement, Duterte's spokesperson Atty. Salvador Paolo Panelo Jr. said the focus should be on questions involving the fairness of the Senate impeachment court, the constitutionality of the conviction threshold, and alleged due process violations.

“These issues raise grave doubts as to whether a conviction by the Senate impeachment court, and any consequent attempt to install a replacement, would rest on any solid legal and moral foundation,” he said.
Panelo raised concerns about the impartiality of senators serving as impeachment court judges, particularly those facing or allegedly threatened with plunder and other criminal charges.

Citing a Social Weather Stations (SWS) survey conducted from September 21 to 27, Panelo said only 28% of Filipinos trust the Senate impeachment court to render a fair judgment, with a net trust rating of -7%.
He questioned again the Senate majority's response to the prosecution's withdrawal of certain impeachment articles, saying the move resulted in a waste of time and public funds.
For him, Duterte was also allegedly deprived of a fair opportunity to refute Articles I and IV of the impeachment complaint.

Panelo said that replacing the Vice President will not solve the country’s most urgent crises like soaring inflation, the worsening Super El Niño which threatens food security, the sharp slowdown in economic growth to a post-pandemic low of 2.3%, and the peso’s daily plunge to record lows.

"The impeachment has only made clear how this administration and its allies prioritize political maneuvering over the issues that matter most to ordinary Filipinos: putting food on the table, keeping the economy afloat, and securing the nation’s future'" Panelo said.
Palace Press Officer Undersecretary Claire Castro earlier said President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. has not discussed or considered a replacement for the Vice President.
Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano earlier urged fellow senators to decline any potential offers for the vice presidency should Duterte be convicted.
Senator Francis "Chiz" Escudero previously declared he would refuse the post due to a conflict of interest as a senator-judge.
Under the Constitution, if the vice presidency becomes vacant, the President nominates a new Vice President who must then be confirmed by a majority vote of both houses of Congress.—AOL, GMA News

articles.title: Hegseth pushes US-ASEAN defense framework as China scales back at talks
articles.summary: As China scales back is presence at talks, Pentagon chief Hegseth lays out a defense pitch .

blocks.text: October 29, 2026 | 9:23am
US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth leaves after attending the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Defence Ministers' Meeting in Cebu on Oct. 28, 2026.
Aaron Favila, pool via AFP

MANILA, Philippines — United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth proposed a new defense framework between the United States and Southeast Asia on Wednesday, October 28, telling the region’s defense chiefs that Washington wants guided cooperation over a “critically important” next several years.
Hegseth made the pitch in his opening remarks at an informal meeting with defense ministers of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

"Next year marks the 50th anniversary formally of US-ASEAN relations, an important milestone, and in recognition of this milestone, we propose that we work together to develop a US-ASEAN framework for defense cooperation, a practical framework that guides our cooperation over the next several years," Hegseth said. "I will note a critically important next several years."
Washington, Hegseth said, was ready to begin work on it with Singapore, which takes over the rotating chairmanship of the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM) from the Philippines this week.
The proposal came as China scaled back its presence at the talks after Beijing decided to send only the defense attaché of its embassy in Manila to Thursday’s ADMM-Plus session.
This is Beijing's lowest level of representation since the defense meetings began in 2010.

Hegseth described the US approach as “strong, quiet, and clear" and said it was meant to be strong enough to deter coercion and quiet enough to avoid escalation, while leaving partners and potential adversaries in no doubt about where Washington stands.

"We're not going to agree on everything, nor do we need to, but an agreement on the fundamentals is enough to support practical cooperation where our shared interests are overlapping and are clear, and that's the type of cooperation the Department of War will continue to pursue with our ASEAN partners," he said.

Hegseth identified maritime domain awareness, interoperability and closer cooperation among navies as priorities for the Department of War, the name the Trump administration now uses for the Pentagon.
In May, Hegseth praised the Philippines, Japan, South Korea and Australia for raising defense spending and warned of consequences for nations that rely on others for their security.
Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr., who chaired the meeting, said a robust US presence was “necessary for peace and stability in Southeast Asia and in the broader Indo-Pacific region.”

articles.title: Personal data of 40,000 U.S. Homeland Security employees leaked in security breach
articles.summary: The leak website Distributed Denial of Secrets said on ‌Wednesday it has released data on more than 40,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees, including details about officials working in…

image.caption: The seal of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security is seen at a 2021 news conference. The personal data of 40,000 DHS employees has been leaked as part of a cybersecurity breach. (Marco Bello/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New

The leak website Distributed Denial of Secrets said on ‌Wednesday it has released data on more than 40,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees, including details about officials working in sensitive fields such as surveillance and human intelligence.
Security breaches at FBI and U.S. War Department have also been exposed in the past month

The leak website Distributed Denial of Secrets said on ‌Wednesday it has released data on more than 40,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) employees, including details about officials working in sensitive fields such as surveillance and human intelligence.

DHS said in a statement it was "aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively." The agency said it was working to ensure its employees ​were properly protected and would update the public "when more information is ​available.”

The disclosure — which the non-profit data transparency group says draws on information obtained by an entity calling itself "Department of Peace" — is the third major government data leak to have made headlines in the past month.

In ​September, the hacking group ShinyHunters claimed the theft of a massive trove of data from the Federal ⁠Bureau of Investigation (FBI), including sensitive job ⁠details and medical information from thousands of bureau employees. Last week, ‌the U.S. War Department was hit with a class-action lawsuit following a breach that exposed data on millions of current and former military personnel.

items: ShinyHunters hackers say they won't leak sensitive FBI data
Dutch police arrest security professional in ShinyHunters investigation

blocks.text: The DHS data includes names, phone numbers and email addresses of employees from Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Customs and Border Protection, Homeland Security Investigations, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, and other DHS component agencies.

Also included in ⁠the data were job titles and email groups, which, among other details, showed which agents were assigned to special operations, surveillance jobs, computer forensics and undercover work.
Canadian ransomware negotiator arrested in connection to FBI hacking case

In a statement, Distributed Denial of Secrets co-founder Emma Best said the hacktivist known as "maia arson crimew" developed a search tool for ‌the data that would allow the public to browse it. Best said the tool would "replace anonymity with accountability" and empower journalists, guide public records requests and boost congressional oversight.

The Department of Peace did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but in a statement included with the data it said that DHS employees "have our information, so it's only fair that ​we have theirs" and that it hoped the data "can be used to limit further harm by the DHS and supports all efforts in that direction."

items: What drives ShinyHunters, the group that claimed responsibility for hacking the FBI?

blocks.text: The Department of Peace in ⁠March claimed responsibility for hacking DHS and posting documents related to contracts with outside vendors.

Best's statement said the Department of Peace harvested ⁠the data from the Okta sign-on service used by DHS. Reuters could not immediately corroborate the claim. Okta said in response to ⁠a Reuters ⁠query: "Okta is secure, and we have no evidence our ​data or systems were compromised."
Caught in a data breach? 3 tips for what to do next

Reuters could not immediately verify the authenticity of the entire data trove but it was able to match ​personal information about six DHS employees named ⁠in the leak to credit bureau records and breach data carried by the dark web intelligence platform District 4 Labs. Reuters called three DHS employees directly and was able to confirm their phone numbers and other details. One said it was the first they had heard of a breach.

In several cases, the data tracked information available on DHS employees' LinkedIn profiles. But in others, the data revealed non-public data about internal DHS ⁠organization charts or previously undisclosed programs or ‌operations.

articles.title: Polls closing in municipal elections across Manitoba
articles.summary: Voters are awaiting results as polls are closing in municipal elections across Manitoba.

blocks.text: Manitoba·New
Voters are awaiting results as polls are closing in municipal elections across Manitoba.
No shortage of races, but some areas have already elected leaders by acclamation
CBC Manitoba’s 2026 municipal election night special
Voters are awaiting results as polls have started to close in municipal elections across Manitoba.
People who are in line to vote before polls officially close at 8 p.m. are still eligible to cast a ballot.
In Winnipeg, there are 12 candidates running for mayor, including incumbent Scott Gillingham.
The last sitting mayor to suffer an election-night defeat in the city was George Sharpe, who came up short in a narrow loss to Independent MLA Stephen Juba in 1956.

A recent public opinion survey suggested that although Gillingham had more support than any other candidate, his early and seemingly insurmountable lead was nearly halved about a week before election day.

items: Mayoral election results in Manitoba

blocks.text: A former city councillor, Gillingham won his first term as mayor in 2022. He squeaked by on election night with 27.5 per cent of the popular vote, repelling a comeback bid by former mayor Glen Murray to win by only 4,391 votes.

Gillingham, Winnipeg Sun CEO Kevin Klein and funeral director Mike Vogiatzakis, the front-runners in early polling, were the candidates eligible to participate in CBC Manitoba's Oct. 21 mayoral debate.
Scott Gillingham, centre, goes head-to-head with Kevin Klein, right, and Mike Vogiatzakis in a televised debate hosted by CBC Manitoba on Oct. 21. (James Turner/CBC)
There are 54 council candidates and more than 90 school trustee candidates in Winnipeg, the city said.
There will be at least five new people on Winnipeg's city council, after five veteran councillors did not seek re-election.

Eyes are also on the councillor's seat in Transcona, where incumbent Russ Wyatt sought re-election while facing criminal charges, including sexual assault, which police say involve two men in separate incidents from 2023 and 2025.
All Winnipeg races were contested this year; in 2022, two councillors won re-election by acclamation.

Voter turnout in the city has waxed and waned in Winnipeg's six elections since 2002. The 2022 election that saw Gillingham first elected mayor recorded a 37.5 per cent voter turnout — the lowest since 2006.

items: What promises have Winnipeg's 2026 mayoral candidates made on key issues?

blocks.text: Voter turnout was much higher in 2014, when Brian Bowman was first elected mayor, with 50 per cent of electors casting ballots.
This year, a record number of Winnipeggers took advantage of advance voting to cast their ballot, the city said.
Elections outside of Winnipeg
Manitobans outside of Winnipeg also voted for new leaders and councils.
Incumbent mayors in several Manitoba communities, including Portage la Prairie, Steinbach, Winkler, Niverville and Selkirk, were acclaimed after no challengers registered to run.
Several places, such as the Municipality of Cartwright-Roblin and the Rural Municipality of Argyle, saw their entire slate of council candidates acclaimed.
Two veteran politicians who served with each other on Brandon city council are battling to become mayor of Manitoba's second-largest city.

Incumbent Jeff Fawcett was elected Brandon mayor four years ago, after serving on council for three terms. His opponent, Len Isleifson, is also a former city councillor and was MLA for Brandon East from 2016 to 2023.

Advance voting in the Wheat City also set a new record in 2026, with more than triple the number of advance votes cast in 2022, far exceeding any advance poll held in the city in the last 20 years, officials said previously.

items: Here's what you need to know ahead of Manitoba's municipal election vote on Wednesday

blocks.text: Up north, residents in Flin Flon voted for a new mayor after Mayor George Fontaine did not run again. Three names were on the mayoral ballot in Flin Flon.
In The Pas, three candidates are also battling for an open mayor's seat. The northern town has been without a mayor since August, after Andre Murphy stepped down from the job.
Incumbent Colleen Smook faced two challengers in Thompson's mayoral race.
Three Manitoba communities — Winnipeg Beach, Victoria Beach and Dunnottar — held elections earlier this year. Only one mayor — Penny McMorris, the incumbent in Victoria Beach — was acclaimed.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

articles.title: Albania imposes $6,000 fine for demonstrators present at a protest that turns violent
articles.summary:
The fine – six times the average monthly salary – will apply to people present at violent protests, even if they don’t personally commit violent acts

Albania has introduced fines of more…

blocks.text: Albania has introduced fines of more than $6,000 for demonstrators who participate in a protest that turns violent, even if they don’t personally commit violent acts, as the government tries to clamp down on the gatherings calling for the prime minister’s resignation.
The capital, Tirana, has been racked by months of anti-government protests that in recent days have deteriorated into pitched battles between the security forces and protesters.
The leaderless movement started peacefully in May, with rallies against a luxury hotel project in a nature reserve, backed by US president Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner.

It morphed in mid-October into a wave of student-led protests against perceived corruption, shortcomings in the health system and the lack of prospects for young people in the country of 2.3 million people.

On Wednesday, prime minister Edi Rama’s government adopted legislative measures imposing fines of up to 500,000 leks (€5,500, US$6,130) for “anyone who chooses to remain in a crowd” that is carrying out acts of violence or looting in a public space, or “concealing their identity”.

blocks.caption: Police detain a protester during an anti-government rally in Tirana on Sunday. Photograph: Hameraldi Agolli/AP

blocks.text: The average salary before tax in Albania is €930 (US$1,026) per month.

Police were also given powers to temporarily restrict gatherings in certain areas, including near educational, healthcare and government institutions if there was a risk of violence. The measures also provide for sanctions against online incitement to violence and compensation for small businesses damaged during protests.
The measures take immediate effect but must be approved by parliament within 45 days to remain in force.

Rama said on Sunday that he was inspired by a French bill, passed by the parliament’s upper house on Wednesday, that would make protesters financially liable for damage caused during street demonstrations.
The prime minister has repeatedly blamed “foreign actors” for the violence and accused both Russia and Iran of driving online misinformation. Rama has also called for “dialogue”.
With Agence France-Presse and Reuters

articles.title: EU countries block Canada's 'associate membership' plan
articles.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen wanted to give Canada a special status within the EU. But Germany and other member states have raised objections ahead of a summit in Montreal.

image.caption: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen are seeking closer ties between Canada and the EU [FILE: September 16, 2026]Image: Justin Tang/The Canadian Press/AP Photo/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: European Union member states have blocked a proposal by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to grant Canada a special status as an "associate member" of the bloc.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and several other EU leaders pushed to remove the term from a draft declaration ahead of a two-day EU-Canada summit beginning Thursday in Montreal, according to diplomats cited by the dpa and AFP news agencies.
Instead, the revised document calls for a plan to establish "closer ties" between Canada and the EU without membership.

blocks.caption: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney met German Chancellor Friedrich Merz at the Chancellery in Berlin in August 2025 [FILE: August 26, 2025]Image: Annegret Hilse/REUTERS

blocks.text: The declaration was approved by EU member states on Wednesday evening and is expected to be published on Friday, at the end of the summit.
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, von der Leyen, European Council President Antonio Costa and several EU commissioners are attending the talks.
Why did EU countries oppose Canada's associate membership?
Von der Leyen first proposed making Canada the EU's first "associate member" in September during a speech attended by Carney.
Canada's PM welcomes EU associate membership idea
However, the proposal raised questions among member states because existing EU treaties do not provide for such a status.
Diplomats said several governments were concerned about the lack of clarity surrounding the proposed arrangement and insufficient consultation between the European Commission and EU member states.
Germany, France and Italy were among the countries that raised objections, although they broadly support closer cooperation with Canada.
Another concern was that the term "associate membership" had already been used in discussions about Ukraine's potential accession to the EU.

Merz had previously suggested such a status for Ukraine as an intermediate step toward full membership. Under his proposal, Kyiv could participate in EU summits and ministerial meetings without voting rights.
Von der Leyen, however, used the same term to describe a different arrangement for Canada, a country that does not have a legal path to EU membership.

blocks.caption: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed making Canada an "associate member" of the EU during a speech at the European Parliament in Strasbourg in September [FILE: September 16, 2026]Image: Yves Herman/REUTERS

blocks.text: An earlier draft of the summit declaration would have allowed Canada to participate in consultations on major EU political and regulatory initiatives as an associate member.
It also called for the full scope of the arrangement to be defined by the 2027 EU-Canada summit.
Carney, meanwhile, played down the dispute over the wording of the summit declaration.
He said the precise terminology mattered less than the practical benefits closer cooperation would bring to Canadians.
What will closer EU-Canada cooperation involve?
Despite the disagreement over terminology, both sides intend to significantly deepen their partnership.
The revised declaration focuses on an "Alliance for the Future," a term Carney has frequently used to describe relations between Canada and the EU.
The initiative aims to remove trade barriers, facilitate investment and secure supplies of critical raw materials, medicines and technologies during crises.
As Trump menaces, some think Canada should join the EU
Both sides also want to strengthen cooperation on energy, climate protection, artificial intelligence, security and education.
Canada could gain broader access to EU programs covering research, education and defense.
A new economic council is planned to bring together businesses from both sides of the Atlantic.
The declaration also calls for a study into the feasibility of increasing Canadian liquefied natural gas exports to Europe.
However, EU governments watered down several economic commitments in the original draft.

An explicit goal of deeper financial market integration was removed. Instead of promising preferential treatment in economic security measures, both sides now intend to limit potential negative effects on each other.
How has Donald Trump affected EU-Canada relations?
The push for closer ties comes amid growing uncertainty over relations with the United States under President Donald Trump.
Trade disputes, US tariffs and Trump's territorial claims have raised concerns in both Canada and Europe about Washington's reliability as a partner.
Both sides hope that closer cooperation will help reduce their dependence on other countries and strengthen their ability to pursue common interests.
How could Trump react to Canada-EU association plan?
Trump previously dismissed the idea of Canadian associate membership in the EU as ridiculous.
He also threatened consequences if the arrangement harmed US interests, warning that he could impose high tariffs or halt trade with Europe in several sectors.

articles.title: Judge rebuffs Trump DoJ’s bid to order California to set aside 20,000 ballots
articles.summary:
Justice department had demanded state segregate ballots from people it claimed were non-citizens

A federal judge

blocks.text: A federal judge declined to order California election officials to segregate ballots from people the Trump administration claimed were non-citizens, rebuffing a legally thin request from the justice department that appeared designed to cast doubt over the results of the midterms.

The ruling from US district judge David Carter, nominated to the federal bench by Bill Clinton, comes about two weeks after the justice department delivered a USB drive to election officials in Los Angeles and Sacramento that it said contained the names of 20,000 non-citizens on the state’s voter rolls. There are more than 23 million registered voters in California and non-citizen voting is extremely rare.

“This case is about the right of every American citizen to vote in a free and fair election,” Carter wrote in his Wednesday evening ruling. “Never before in American history has the federal government, on the eve of an election, sought to coerce a state and local government to abandon their own Constitutional elections procedures and bend to the will of the Executive Branch.”
“In bringing this lawsuit, the Executive would have this Court believe that it reigns as a sole sovereign,” Carter continued. “But California and its people are sovereign, too.”

The justice department gave officials just 48 hours to review the list and said it would sue the state if officials did not sequester ballots from those whose citizenship it could not confirm. The department refused to provide more details about its methodology and Los Angeles officials found preliminary indicators the list was inaccurate. The justice department then sued California on 15 October to try and force the state to sequester the ballots and verify citizenship.

The justice department separately has threatened to prosecute election officials in the state if they tabulate ballots from non-citizens. Such a move would be without a legal basis, Sam Trepel, a former prosecutor at the justice department, wrote in a blogpost this month. After filing the lawsuit, the Trump administration began providing lists to other counties of suspected non-citizen voters. When election officials began reviewing them, they found the department had flagged voters who were not on the rolls and had provided insufficient information to verify their citizenship status, according to CalMatters.

Carter’s ruling came after the justice department tried to bypass him entirely. After Carter set a 27 October hearing on the justice department’s emergency motion, the department took the unusual step of appealing to the US court of appeals for the ninth circuit, saying Carter was not considering the case fast enough. A panel of ninth circuit judges ruled 2-1 against the justice department earlier this week.

Legal experts have been skeptical about the justice department’s efforts in California since the outset. In July, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced it had identified up to 190,000 non-citizens on California voter rolls. The DHS did not provide more details to the state until after ballots had already gone out in the state.

articles.title: What’s at stake for Trump in Israel’s deadlocked election?
articles.summary: The outcome will have implications for US-Israeli relations, which have been dominated by the joint fight against Iran, stalled Gaza peace efforts and signs of eroding US public support for Israel

blocks.text: TRUMP AND NETANYAHU. US President Donald Trump welcomes Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the entrance of the White House in Washington, DC, USA, April 7, 2025.
Leah Millis/Reuters
The outcome will have implications for US-Israeli relations, which have been dominated by the joint fight against Iran, stalled Gaza peace efforts and signs of eroding US public support for Israel

items: Israel's recent election resulted in no clear winner, leading to uncertainty for President Trump regarding US-Israeli relations amid ongoing challenges from Iran and Gaza.

Prime Minister Netanyahu's bloc secured the most seats but lacks a parliamentary majority, setting the stage for potential coalition negotiations or another election while he remains in a caretaker role.
The election outcome may impact Trump's strategy against Iran and hinder progress on Gaza peace efforts, as both potential leaders maintain tough stances on security and negotiations.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

WASHINGTON, USA – With Israel’s election yielding no clear winner, President Donald Trump could face prolonged uncertainty over who will lead Washington’s closest Middle East ally as he confronts challenges from Iran and Gaza across the region.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right-wing bloc secured the most seats in Israel’s parliament but still lost its parliamentary majority on Tuesday, October 27, despite Trump having endorsed him against a rival alliance of parties led by hawkish former military chief Gadi Eisenkot.

While Netanyahu seemed in a stronger position, neither side was projected to have an outright path to form a new government after Israel’s first election since the Hamas-led attacks of October 7, 2023, and the ensuing wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.

blocks.caption: Netanyahu set to remain caretaker after inconclusive Israeli election

blocks.text: The stage appeared to be set for a period of painstaking coalition bargaining – or possibly another election – while Netanyahu remains in power in a caretaker capacity.
The outcome will have implications for US-Israeli relations, which have been dominated by the joint fight against Iran, stalled Gaza peace efforts and signs of eroding US public support for Israel.
The uncertainty comes at a sensitive moment for Trump, when he and Netanyahu have threatened to join in another round of attacks against Iran.

“Israeli politics can be messy,” said Aaron David Miller, a former Middle East adviser in Democratic and Republican administrations. From the US perspective, he said, “it would be good to get some clarity, but that’s easier said than done.”

Netanyahu – a consummate political survivor who has had a close but sometimes turbulent relationship with Trump dating back decades – may have survived again. He is the longest-serving Israeli prime minister and the only one the US president has ever worked with.

Eisenkot, who projected an image as a ⁠political outsider and security-minded former general during the campaign, has seen his governing chances dimmed but not extinguished. He is not known to have ever met Trump.

Some analysts say creation of a broad unity government keeping Netanyahu in power might serve Trump’s interest in a politically stable Israeli partner. But neither side has shown a willingness to take that path.
Asked whether he was going to get involved in an effort to form a Netanyahu-led unity government, Trump told Axios on Wednesday he hadn’t thought about it, adding: “I will take a look.”

Topping the list is how Trump might engage with Israel in the war against Iran, which has rocked the Middle East. The eight-month-old conflict has disrupted global energy supplies, pushed up US gasoline prices and driven down his approval ratings, imperiling his Republicans’ control of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections.

Trump, in his October 18 endorsement, insisted he wanted Netanyahu to remain in power to help him soon “finish the job” against Iran. The president said overnight that Netanyahu, who outperformed pre-election polls, had done “very well” and that his backing had boosted the Israeli leader.

Trump has repeatedly signaled that the US and Israel could restart attacks on Iran after the midterms, with some critics, including in Israel, suggesting Netanyahu might see it as a way to bolster his political standing as caretaker prime minister.

Jonathan Panikoff, a former deputy US national intelligence officer on the Middle East, said any future Israeli leadership would likely be on the same page as Trump if he decides to escalate from the current stalemate with Israel’s regional arch-foe.
“It’s hard to imagine any real daylight between them on that point,” said Panikoff, now at the Atlantic Council think tank in Washington.
Where Netanyahu and many Israelis have sometimes differed with Trump is when he has offered concessions in now-stalled negotiations with the Islamic Republic.
No matter how Israel’s next government shapes up, there is little reason to believe there will be any sweeping shift in tough policies toward the Palestinians.

This doesn’t bode well for breaking the diplomatic deadlock between Israel and Hamas and fully implementing Trump’s Gaza peace plan following the war there. Israel, in response to the militants’ deadly cross-border attack, leveled much of the enclave and killed tens of thousands of Palestinians.
Administration officials have privately expressed frustration over what they see as intransigence by Netanyahu, who has insisted that Hamas must first disarm.

Eisenkot, who lost a son and two nephews in the Gaza war, stressed his military credentials while positioning himself as a centrist domestically during the election campaign. He has vowed to break with Netanyahu’s far-right coalition allies, but not with the hawkish approach to security that has become more entrenched since the 2023 Hamas attack. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Netanyahu set to remain caretaker after inconclusive Israeli election
articles.summary: While a caretaker government faces some constraints, experts say it retains powers, including over the war with Iran

blocks.text: UN ADDRESS. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu holds up a Starlink device as he addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City, US, September 24, 2026.
While a caretaker government faces some constraints, experts say it retains powers, including over the war with Iran

items: Benjamin Netanyahu is likely to remain Israel's caretaker prime minister despite his right-wing bloc losing its parliamentary majority, as they are projected to win 53 seats compared to 48 for the opposition.

The election results indicate a significant rightward shift among Israeli Jews, with nearly all Jewish parties rejecting the idea of an independent Palestinian state, and Arab parties winning an unprecedented 19 seats.

Netanyahu's government faces challenges, including accusations of using security issues for political gain, and the political landscape is further complicated by ongoing conflicts and high voter turnout among Arab Israelis.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

JERUSALEM, Israel – Benjamin Netanyahu looked set to remain Israel’s caretaker prime minister after unexpectedly strong backing among Jewish voters left his opponents little apparent prospect of unseating him, despite his right-wing bloc losing its parliamentary majority.

With nearly 86% of votes tallied on Wednesday, Israel’s three main broadcasters projected Netanyahu’s bloc of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties would win 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, well ahead of the 48 for rival Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition bloc.

Parties representing Arab Israelis were projected to win an unprecedented 19 seats, leaving Eisenkot little realistic path to power without their broad backing, which many Jewish political leaders reject.

blocks.caption: Israeli exit polls show deadlock, setback for Netanyahu

blocks.text: The results could still change as counting continued, but Eisenkot’s bloc of anti-Netanyahu parties, ranging from the center-left to the hard right, had fallen short of pre-election polls that forecast a tight race.

Netanyahu would remain caretaker prime minister during any coalition negotiations and potentially until another election next year. While a caretaker government faces some constraints, experts say it retains powers, including over the war with Iran.

Guy Lurie, a research fellow at the Israel Democracy Institute, said a caretaker government formally had the same powers as a regular government, but also “a duty of restraint” and less discretion in some areas.
Netanyahu, addressing his Likud party’s faithful after 3 am (0100 GMT), called for the formation of “a strong, right-wing national government.”

He highlighted Israel’s military successes and raised the prospect of renewed joint military action against Iran alongside his ally, US President Donald Trump, saying the two countries had a “singular historical opportunity” to remove what he called the Iranian threat “once and for all.”

Trump, who had urged Israeli voters to keep Netanyahu in power so the two leaders could “finish the job” in Iran, said Netanyahu had done “very well” and claimed his endorsement had “helped him a lot.”
Israel’s high-turnout vote was brushed aside by some in the rest of the Middle East.

In Tehran, banners with images of slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei reminded Iranians of US and Israeli strikes launched in February which kicked off the war. Just to the right was a poster of late Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah, who was killed on Netanyahu’s orders in Lebanon.
“I genuinely see the possibility of attack,” said 50-year-old Iranian citizen Abdollah Karimi.
Frustration was also palpable in Egypt, the first Arab country to make peace with Israel in 1979.
Outhman Selim, a 62-year-old lawyer, said his hopes that a Netanyahu defeat would steer the country away from the far right had been dashed.
Eisenkot acknowledged that Netanyahu remained caretaker prime minister but warned that he might use security for political ends.

“I call on the heads of the security establishment and the civil service: Netanyahu is a caretaker prime minister, without a mandate or the people’s trust,” he said. “Stand firm in the face of any attempt to challenge you.”
Netanyahu’s office has previously rejected accusations that he is using the Iran conflict for political gain and did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Wednesday.

The prospect of a caretaker government without a parliamentary majority weighed on Israeli markets. The shekel ILS= currency weakened around 1.6% to 3.10 to the US dollar. Tel Aviv’s key benchmark stock indexes fell more than 3%.

The result underscored the rightward shift among Israeli Jews during Netanyahu’s years as the country’s dominant political figure. The center-left that dominated Israel for the first half of its history has been reduced to a small fringe.
Nearly all Jewish parties now share Netanyahu’s rejection of an eventual independent Palestinian state, the basis of internationally endorsed peace efforts since the 1990s.
The election was Israel’s first since Hamas-led fighters killed 1,200 people and took 251 hostages in attacks on October 7, 2023, that plunged the country into wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.
The war in Gaza, which flattened the territory and killed 74,000 Palestinians, according to Gaza health authorities, has left Israel increasingly isolated on the world stage.
Netanyahu himself is wanted by the International Criminal Court in The Hague on war crimes charges he calls absurd, and faces corruption charges in Israel that he dismisses as an establishment plot.

Turnout reached 77.7%, the highest in more than two decades, and was particularly high among Israelis of Palestinian descent, who make up more than a fifth of the population. Many were motivated by what they see as open racism from Netanyahu’s cabinet, which includes a party leader convicted of inciting racial hatred against Arabs.

The headquarters of the Joint List, an alliance of several Arab parties, burst into whistles and applause when exit polls were released. “We refuse the occupation and racism, and we will remain here,” said Joint List candidate Faten Gattas.

The coalition that last toppled Netanyahu relied on one small Arab party, but Eisenkot’s underperformance means the opposition would now need backing from the Joint List itself. Most Jewish leaders have shunned formal alliances with Arab parties since Israel’s founding. – Rappler.com

The ADMM-Plus expands defense cooperation to eight dialogue partners including Australia, China, India, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia, and the United States. —VAL, GMA News
